idea-repo.responsibility: Discover research directions: survey what is already known, identify a concrete tractable question, and record a candidate idea.

story-repo.responsibility: Design the research story: state the proposed contribution, narrative and logic, and plan hypotheses/comparisons to test or falsify with experiments, figures and tables. The story may be designed before results exist, but the final narrative must follow actual evidence, including null or negative findings, not require a winning conclusion. Preserve the source objective issue reference and its unmodified constraints from idea in PLAN.md and downstream handoffs; relay idea and idea-review release evidence to paper with full SHAs and file provenance.

idea-review-repo.responsibility: Review whether the idea is worth doing under the current resource and time constraints: check overlap with existing work and estimate implementation cost. Reject or bound the scope when it is unrealistic.

experiment-repo.responsibility: Implement and execute the study: write runnable code, execute it, and commit real results with commands, configuration, fixed seeds and a reproducible procedure. World measurements may reuse prior committed executions with exact commit/file/run provenance; sourced facts and explicit planning estimates follow the shared evidence rules and need not be executions you personally ran. Generate every result row from executed scripts, never hand-transcribe or invent rows. Script derived percentages with their explicit numerator and denominator; uncertainty claims require the estimator, sample unit/count, repetition/seed scheme and script-derived intervals or dispersion. Test or falsify the planned hypotheses and comparisons without prescribing a winning conclusion; report null, negative and contradictory findings honestly.

figtab-repo.responsibility: Turn committed experimental evidence into figures and tables, with the generator committed alongside its output so both can be regenerated. Obtain venue formats/dimensions and paper's embedding/build interface; deliver the required formats alongside the canonical SVG and table, exact paths, captions, units, source result commit/file references and generator command. Confirm paper can embed them in its actual submission format, not merely mention their filenames.
deliverables: table.csv, table.tex or table.md (may be nested)
the generator script (Python, R, shell or Julia)

venue-repo.responsibility: Choose a plausible venue and record scope match, format, length and review criteria in VENUE.md. Record each guideline's URL, version/date, actual access date and retrieval outcome plus the relevant excerpt. Recalled guidance is provisional, not a successful retrieval; disclose unavailable sources and obtain verifiable requirements before final approval. Commit venue-artifacts.json with `{"artifact_schema":1,"required_paper_files":["submission/manuscript.pdf"]}` using exact paper-relative paths for all sources, templates and rendered artifacts the chosen venue actually requires. The list may be empty only if verified venue requirements require no supplementary artifacts; explain in VENUE.md. Do not impose LaTeX universally. Send paper and figtab explicit dimensions, file formats, embedding and build/template requirements with source provenance.

paper-repo.responsibility: Integrate the story, executed evidence, figures/tables and venue constraints into a manuscript, and revise it in response to internal review. paper.md is the canonical manuscript, not a substitute for venue-specific submission sources, PDF or template. Include all supplementary paths declared by venue's venue-artifacts.json, with reproducible build instructions. Obtain exact formatting requirements from venue and compatible figure/table outputs from figtab; embed and check the actual figures, not merely filenames or links to absent files. Label provisional Markdown-only handoffs as drafts, not submission-ready artifacts. You own the manuscript: review every pull request opened against your repository and merge it or close it with a stated reason. Leaving one open is not a decision.
deliverables: venue-required submission sources, template and PDF as declared in venue-artifacts.json

internal-review-repo.responsibility: Review the manuscript against its evidence. Check every measured quantitative claim against results committed in `experiment-repo`; verify sourced quantities against their cited source/version and estimates against their explicit assumptions, without presenting either as measured results, and record in `REVIEW.md` which commit and file each claim was checked against; a review that cites no evidence is not a review. Raise concrete findings, propose an exact correction as a pull request when known, and open an issue to the owning position only if it is your direct neighbor. For a nonneighbor (such as figtab, story, idea or idea-review), send the finding and exact commit/file references to paper-repo, your authorized relay; paper routes it along authorized graph edges and returns the owner's response. Never open an off-graph issue or PR or fetch nonneighbor repositories. Track whether revisions address the findings. Recompute quantitative numerator/denominator arithmetic and uncertainty summaries from the recorded scripts/results; verify figure embedding and inspect the actual venue-required rendered format and sources, not just filename presence. Verify guideline retrieval traces distinguish real access from provisional recollection. Models can err: require corrections with evidence, never manufacture measurements or predetermined conclusions. Record formal requested-changes against the paper candidate when requiring revisions; ordinary issue prose is not machine-classified as a revision request. Your revision_required attestation also covers requests made in prose and must not deny any known revision history.
